slides.title: Threats can be **a crime.**
slides.body: Threatening someone "by any means" with injury to their person, reputation or property, meaning to alarm them or make them do what they aren't legally bound to, is criminal intimidation. Threats against someone close count too.

slides.title: What the law **can impose.**
list: Criminal intimidation: up to 2 years, or fine, or both
Threat of death or grievous hurt: up to 7 years
Threat to impute unchastity to a woman: up to 7 years
Each can also be fine alone, or jail plus fine

slides.title: Monitoring a woman online? **Stalking.**
slides.body: A man who monitors a woman's use of the internet, email or any other electronic communication commits stalking. First conviction: up to 3 years and fine. Repeat conviction: up to 5 years and fine.

slides.title: **Save** everything.
slides.body: The government's Cyber Dost guide says to save all communications with a stalker as evidence, end communication, and use the platform's "report and block" option.

slides.title: Report it **online.**
slides.body: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, cybercrime.gov.in, takes reports of all types of cyber crime, with special focus on crimes against women and children. Helpline 1930 helps you lodge a complaint.

slides.title: Police complaint by **e-communication.**
slides.body: Information about a cognizable offence can be given to a police station orally or by electronic communication, wherever the offence happened. An electronic complaint is taken on record once you sign it within 3 days.

sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 78, 351 (indiacode.nic.in; Sec 351 as quoted by the Supreme Court in 2026 INSC 587)

caption:
Being threatened online? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ Threatening someone by any means with injury to person, reputation or property can be criminal intimidation
2️⃣ Punishment: up to 2 years, or fine, or both. Threats to kill or cause grievous hurt: up to 7 years
3️⃣ A man monitoring a woman's internet, email or electronic communication commits stalking
4️⃣ Save all communications as evidence, then report and block
5️⃣ Report on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930
6️⃣ Information about a cognizable offence can be given to police by electronic communication; sign it within 3 days

Source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 78, 351); Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 173); I4C, MHA
